chapters.title: Entropy balances for open systems
chapters.summary: Track entropy carried by heat and flowing matter, identify irreversibility, and test whether a proposed operating state is admissible.

chapters.title: Reversible Steady-Flow Work
chapters.summary: Derive the pressure integral for shaft work, compare compression paths, and use both thermodynamic laws to test real equipment.

chapters.title: Entropy balances in thermal equipment
chapters.summary: Close the mass and energy accounts before interpreting the entropy residual in condensers, mixers, nozzles, and coupled devices.

chapters.title: Work and irreversibility in flow equipment
chapters.summary: Compare actual and reversible reference processes for diffusers, compressors, nozzles, linked shafts, and blowdown.

chapters.title: Exergy and the reference environment
chapters.summary: Derive closed-system availability, distinguish work transfer from energy transfer, and quantify the work lost to entropy generation.

chapters.title: Flow exergy and useful output
chapters.summary: Derive stream availability and apply one exergy account to compressors, turbines, feedwater heaters, and heat engines.

chapters.title: Exergy of closed systems
chapters.summary: Apply the closed-system exergy balance to compression, phase changes, internal equilibration, and moving pistons, then compare the flow tutorial cases.

chapters.title: Exergy of steady and transient control volumes
chapters.summary: Identify the exergy resource and useful product in heaters, turbines, chillers, and changing-mass vessels.

chapters.title: Rankine Cycles
chapters.summary: Reconstruct a steam power cycle, distinguish moisture and efficiency constraints, and quantify how feedwater heating and reheat change the balance.

chapters.title: Brayton Cycles
chapters.summary: Derive the ideal gas-turbine cycle, find its maximum-work pressure ratio, and quantify how actual components and variable heat capacity change the result.

chapters.title: Modified Brayton Cycles
chapters.summary: Quantify how intercooling, reheat, and regeneration interact at fixed compressor inlet temperature, turbine inlet temperature, and overall pressure ratio.

chapters.title: Otto and Diesel Cycles
chapters.summary: Compare ideal spark-ignition and compression-ignition cycles under shared temperature and compression constraints, then relate work to cylinder displacement.

chapters.title: Vapor-Compression Refrigeration
chapters.summary: Reconstruct a vapor-compression cycle from its enthalpies, quantify compressor and exchanger penalties, and separate refrigeration duty from power.

chapters.title: Properties of Moist Air
chapters.summary: Derive humidity ratio, dew point, and enthalpy on a dry-air mass basis, then use phase equilibrium to locate condensation.

chapters.title: Psychrometric Paths
chapters.summary: Read a pressure-specific chart and use water and energy balances for cooling, reheating, mixing, drying, and towers.

chapters.title: Air-Conditioning Tutorials
chapters.summary: Infer state from dew point, test if a coil can stay dry, and distinguish liquid make-up from total water circulation.

chapters.title: Combustion Thermodynamics
chapters.summary: Balance reacting mixtures, compare heating values on a common water reference, and formulate the combustor energy and entropy balances.

chapters.title: Combustion Stoichiometry Tutorials
chapters.summary: Use explicit species assumptions to solve rich combustion, analyze exhaust composition, and infer an equivalence ratio from mass flows.

chapters.title: Combustion Energy Tutorials
chapters.summary: Reconcile heat release with exhaust conditions, estimate frozen flame temperature, and close a reacting equilibrium model.

chapters.title: Compressible flow and the stagnation state
chapters.summary: Derive the acoustic speed, evaluate density changes, and connect local and stagnation properties.

chapters.title: Stagnation pressure and normal shocks
chapters.summary: Use energy and entropy to explain stagnation-pressure changes and derive the compressive shock solution.

chapters.title: Nozzle geometry, choking, and back pressure
chapters.summary: Derive the area–Mach relation and determine how back pressure selects among nozzle flow regimes.

chapters.title: Air and steam nozzle calculations
chapters.summary: Locate a normal shock from back pressure and adapt the nozzle balances to steam properties.
